_comment: THE BATTERIES CANDIDATE LIST, machine-readable so the gap can be REPORTED rather
than narrated. sources/report_candidate_gaps.py reads it and prints what is still
missing on every build.
WHY IT EXISTS. The perimeter admits a site only when the company has confirmed it
and a citable source identifies the works. Both take research, and a dataset in
build-up therefore has two populations: rows that are on file, and candidates that
are not yet. Held only in prose, the second population is a paragraph somebody has
to remember to update. Held here, it is a number the build prints.
A CANDIDATE LEAVES BY BECOMING A ROW. `id` matches the project id it will take in
data/transition/projects.json, and the report treats a candidate whose id is
already a project as landed. Nothing is deleted when that happens: the entry stays
as the record of what was needed, and the report stops asking for it.
`company_source` is a URL or null. `coordinate_source` is one of the values in
sector_map.LOCATION_SOURCE_TYPES or null. Null means outstanding, and outstanding
is the thing this file is for.
Refused candidates are NOT here. This file is the admitted set; what the perimeter
refuses, and why, is in sources/batteries_docket.md, which is the reviewed record.
`company_source_blocked` is the third state. The right document has been found and
named, and the fetcher cannot read it -- a publisher that answers 403 to a datacentre
IP, or a host whose certificate does not match. It is not a missing source and it is
not a usable one: somebody with a browser can close it in a minute, and until they do
the row cannot carry a verbatim quote nobody has read.
TWO CANDIDATES ARRIVED FROM THE FUNDING WORK RATHER THAN FROM THE PERIMETER SWEEP --
NOVO Energy at Gothenburg and Leclanche at Willstatt, both named in the Commission's
Innovation Fund Battery Call. The sweep looked for gigafactories and missed two that a
list of who got money named directly. Worth remembering the next time a sector is built:
the funding trail is a discovery route and not only a money model.

candidates.note: Status and staleness both turn on the June 2026 update: the cornerstone was laid in July 2024, but as of June 2026 only ground preparation is done and AESC's roadmap puts first cells at December 2028. When the row lands it is construction — ground works have begun — with a note that four and a half years separate the cornerstone from the first cell. Not stale by the twelve-month test: the newest source is three months old.
candidates.company_source_blocked: https://www.aesc-group.com/newsInfo?id=<slug> — 'AESC Spain celebrates the laying of the first stone of the battery gigafactory in Navalmoral de la Mata (Cáceres)'. The live URL form is confirmed by the two pages already retrieved; the slug itself is not, so it is not guessed here.

The substitution note therefore stands: this is press relaying a state source, recorded as press.

UNPARKED AND TAKEN DIRECTLY, once the User-Agent declared a contact and the SEC answered. FREYR's FY2023 10-K, filed 29 February 2024, states it: 'In June 2022 … FREYR formally sanctioned the construction of Giga Arctic, a 120,000 square meter gigafactory in Mo i Rana, Norway. In 2023, we substantially completed groundworks and certain foundation structures, erected the initial building and secured and weatherized it, and then suspended work on the planned gigafactory.' Status is paused; the Customer Qualification Plant on the same site is a 13,000 m² qualification line and is refused separately by the pilot clause. NO CAPACITY IN THE FILING — the 10-K states no GWh figure at all — so capacity is outstanding and the row would be admitted on 'a 120,000 square meter gigafactory' being a company description of commercial-scale intent. COORDINATE OUTSTANDING: Nominatim has only Mo Industripark, which is the estate and is refused on the same rule as IAMP and Parc Sagunt II; Overpass was unavailable for a bounding-box sweep and that is the next thing to try.

Company source in hand (elevenes.com), which confirms both the 8 GWh gigafactory and the separate 1 GWh mega-factory. COORDINATE EXHAUSTED: a bounding-box sweep of 400 features across Subotica returns no feature named or operated by ElevenEs. Not outstanding for want of looking.

The coordinate is not absent, as I said last turn; it is behind a document a browser opens. What occupies the parcel now — a data centre — does not bear on where the project was sited.

FOUND BY THE FUNDING WORK, NOT BY THE PERIMETER SWEEP. The Commission's Innovation Fund Battery Call names 'NOVO One – NOVO One Gigafactory, located in Sweden (NOVO Energy)' as one of six awards. NOVO Energy is the Volvo Cars and Northvolt joint venture at Gothenburg; Northvolt's bankruptcy leaves its ownership needing a source. Neither company source nor coordinate has been read, and it is not clear the perimeter admits it until somebody has.

FOUND BY THE FUNDING WORK. The Commission names 'WGF2G – Willstatt GigaFactory 2 GWh, located in Germany (Leclanche)'. Two GWh clears the perimeter's scale rule, so it is a candidate and not a refusal. Neither company source nor coordinate read.
